notes: Paperless-AI works on documents in a Paperless-ngx server; it does not store documents itself. You need a running Paperless-ngx (the Paperless-ngx one-click recipe works, on this server or another) and an API token from it (in Paperless-ngx: your profile, then API Auth Token), plus an AI provider: an OpenAI API key, an Ollama server, Azure OpenAI or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

The whole site sits behind a password gate, the same one as the Vane and SearXNG recipes: a Caddy proxy with HTTP basic authentication, user admin and the generated password shown on the first-run card. This is not optional: in Paperless-AI 3.0.9 the setup form at /setup answers without a login even after setup is done, and submitting it replaces the existing account and the Paperless-ngx connection. Behind the gate only people with the password can reach it.

First visit: after the gate, Paperless-AI opens its setup screen. Enter the Paperless-ngx address (for example https://<your paperless domain>) and its API token, your Paperless-ngx username, the AI provider and its key and model, and the username and password for Paperless-AI's own login. Setup checks the Paperless-ngx connection and makes one test request to the AI provider, so the AI key must already work. Finish setup right after install. Paperless-AI then restarts itself and asks for its own login.

After setup, restart the app once from the panel. Upstream starts the document-chat (RAG) service only when the container starts, and before setup it has no Paperless-ngx connection and stops; the restart brings it up. The first time it runs, it downloads its multilingual embedding model (about 500 MB) to the data volume (HF_HOME=/app/data/huggingface) and indexes your documents.

Settings, the login, the processing history and the search index live in the data volume on /app/data (Paperless-AI's own .env, its SQLite database and the chromadb index), so they survive restarts and re-creates. JWT_SECRET, which signs Paperless-AI's login cookie, is generated by the panel; upstream's fallback is a fixed public string.

Paperless-AI's own API (the x-api-key header, key shown in its settings) is behind the gate too: callers must also send the gate's user and password. The gate removes its Authorization header before the request reaches Paperless-AI.

Automatic processing scans Paperless-ngx on a schedule (every 30 minutes by default) and sends each new document's text to the AI provider you chose, which costs tokens with paid providers. Limit it to tagged documents or switch it off in Settings if you want to try it on a few documents first.

The image is large (about 4.6 GB, Node.js plus a Python service with PyTorch). Like the other recipes with a proxy in front (Vane, SearXNG, Plane), the panel's memory and CPU limits apply to the proxy, the app service; the Paperless-AI container has a fixed 2g.
Upstream says the project is not actively maintained (README, March 2026); 3.0.9 from November 2025 is its latest release.
